issues.description:
[bug-hunt] AI Overview (/ai/overview) — the Weight tile paints its weekly-change trend arrow with a LOSS-BIASED good/bad color that ignores the user’s goal direction, so for a muscle-gain / weight-gain goal it is semantically inverted.

Root cause: weightChangeIndicator() (src/pages/AIOverview.tsx:43-47) hardcodes, regardless of goal_type:
  change < -0.1  -> text-success (green), ArrowDown   (weight DOWN treated as good)
  change >  0.1  -> text-destructive (red), ArrowUp   (weight UP treated as bad)
The returned color is applied to the trend arrow icon at AIOverview.tsx:379 (<WInd className={... wInd.color} />).

Expected: for a user whose goal is to GAIN (goal_type muscle_gain, or goal_weight above current), gaining should read as ON-TRACK (green) and losing as OFF-TRACK. The primary Dashboard weight card is already goal-progress-framed (start->now->goal milestone track, QA i-20260617-86ba) and is NOT loss-biased; this tile diverges.

Actual: a weight-gain user who successfully gains sees a RED (destructive) up-arrow implying the gain is bad; if they lose weight they get a GREEN “good” down-arrow. Color is the good/bad state signal here and it is wrong-signed for the entire gaining segment.

Repro: use an account with goal_type = muscle_gain (or goal_weight > current). Have weight_summary.change_this_week_kg > 0.1 (a real weekly gain). Open /ai/overview -> the Weight tile’s trend arrow renders red/destructive even though the gain is the desired direction (and a loss would render green).

Fix: make weightChangeIndicator goal-aware — take the goal direction (from dashboard-overview / profile goal_type or goal vs current weight) and map toward-goal -> success, away-from-goal -> destructive, near-zero -> neutral. The text label (↑/↓ x kg this week) can stay; only the color semantics must follow the goal. Low severity: color-only, the number itself is correct; IST/loss-goal users unaffected.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Dashboard Sleep card + its embedded 7-day chart render the night’s DATE LABEL one day early for users in negative-UTC (Americas) timezones.

Root cause: date labels are built with new Date("YYYY-MM-DD"), which parses a bare date string as UTC midnight; toLocaleDateString / the recency compare then shift it back a day in any timezone west of UTC.
- DashboardSleepCard.recencyLabel  (src/pages/_components/dashboard/DashboardSleepCard.tsx:26)  ->  new Date(latestDate).toLocaleDateString(...)
- SleepQualityChart.formatLabel    (src/components/charts/SleepQualityChart.tsx:32)             ->  new Date(dateStr).toLocaleDateString(...)  (every X-axis label)

Expected: a night logged/synced on Jul 16 shows "Jul 16".
Actual (e.g. America/Los_Angeles, UTC-7): shows "Jul 15"; the Today/Last-night recency check can also mis-classify near midnight.

The codebase already fixed this exact class elsewhere: DashboardFastingCard uses new Date(`${date}T00:00:00`) (local) and lib/cycle.ts uses Date.UTC on split parts. The newer sleep code (i-20260716-sl33) reintroduced the naive parse.

Same naive pattern (wrong WEEKDAY label) also in: src/components/charts/StepsActivityChart.tsx:26, MacroAdherenceChart.tsx:26, CalorieBalanceChart.tsx:26.

Fix: parse the YYYY-MM-DD as local before formatting (append T00:00:00, or split+Date.UTC then format) — ideally add a shared parseLocalDate() helper in src/lib/date.ts and use it in all label formatters. Correct for IST (UTC+5:30) today, so India users are unaffected; only surfaces west of UTC.

Repro: set browser/device TZ to America/Los_Angeles, log or Health-Connect-sync sleep for 2+ days, open /dashboard — the Sleep card’s most-recent date reads one day earlier than logged.

Fix: added a parseLocalDate() helper that builds the date from local calendar parts, and used it in all eight chart/card label formatters (Sleep card + Sleep/Steps/Macro/Calorie/Weight/Measurement charts). Verified by rendering the real charts under a forced America/Los_Angeles timezone: the last day now correctly reads 'Jul 16' / 'Thu'.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Measurements ignores an imperial user’s unit_preference when the profile cache is cold — the cm/inch default fix is incomplete.

What’s wrong: src/pages/Measurements.tsx seeds the unit toggle ONCE at mount by reading the React-Query cache for key [profile-basic-info] (L78-81): cached?.unit_preference === imperial ? inch : cm. But this component never FETCHES [profile-basic-info] — it queries [user-profile] (L95-99, profileService.getProfile) and [measurements-overview]. There is NO effect that re-derives `unit` once the profile resolves. So when the [profile-basic-info] cache is empty at mount, an imperial user is shown centimetres and stays on cm until they manually toggle.

Expected vs actual: An imperial (unit_preference=imperial) user opening Measurements should default to inch. Actual: defaults to cm whenever [profile-basic-info] wasn’t already cached by a prior screen.

The recent fix (commit 595b3015 “Measurements cm/inch default respects unit_preference”, +5/-1 lines) added only the cache read — it works when the cache is warm (e.g. after visiting Profile/LogWeight which DO fetch that key) but does nothing on a cold cache. The comment on L77 claims it ‘mirrors LogWeight.tsx’, but LogWeight actually (a) fetches [profile-basic-info] itself (LogWeight.tsx L158-162) AND (b) has a one-shot sync effect (L224-233, `unitInitDone` ref) that calls handleUnitChange(lb) once profileData loads imperial. Measurements copied the cache-init but not the fetch + sync, so it self-corrects only by luck of a warm cache.

Repro: cold app start (or hard refresh) navigating directly to /measurements as an imperial user, with no prior screen having loaded [profile-basic-info] → toggle shows cm. Note: saved values are always canonical cm so no data corruption; this is a display-default bug.

Fix: mirror LogWeight fully — read unit_preference from the [user-profile] query this component already runs (or fetch [profile-basic-info]) and set `unit` in a one-shot effect when the profile resolves, guarded so it never overrides a manual toggle.

fix.description: Root cause: ChoosePlan computed the weight delta as Math.max(0, current − goal), which clamps to 0 for a weight-GAIN goal — so the header read 'up to 0 kg' and the recommended-plan badge showed '0 kg'. Verified live on /choose-plan with a 70→80 kg gain goal: the header now reads 'up to 10 kg to gain' and the badge '10 kg', with a rising projection.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Choose Plan shows “up to 0 kg” in the header and a “0 kg” badge for weight-GAIN / muscle-gain goals.

What’s wrong: src/pages/ChoosePlan.tsx L403 computes kgsToLose = hasWeightProjection ? Math.max(0, currentWeightKg - goalWeightKg) : 0. For a gain goal (goalWeightKg > currentWeightKg) that subtraction is negative and Math.max clamps it to 0. That 0 is then rendered in two user-visible places:
  • Header (L912-914): t(choose_plan.header.title_with_goal, { count: Math.round(kgsToLose) }) → en.json L1407 “Pick your plan · up to {{count}} kg” → “Pick your plan · up to 0 kg”.
  • Recommended-card badge (L1046): {Math.round(kgsToLose)} kg → “0 kg”.

Expected vs actual: A user whose goal is to gain (e.g. current 70 kg → goal 80 kg) should see their 10 kg journey (or neutral copy), not “up to 0 kg”. The projection chart just below is direction-correct (it plots current→goal as a rising curve and its aria uses a loss/change split, L1171), so the header contradicts the chart on the same screen.

Repro: onboard/set a weight-gain or muscle-gain goal with current < goal weight, reach /choose-plan (paywall) → header reads “Pick your plan · up to 0 kg” and the recommended card badge reads “0 kg”. Loss goals are unaffected (positive delta).

Root cause: kgsToLose is loss-biased. Fix: use Math.abs(currentWeightKg - goalWeightKg) for the magnitude and make the header/badge copy direction-aware (lose vs gain), or hide the “up to X kg” framing for gain/maintain goals.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Body Measurements save-failure handler calls an undefined function -> ReferenceError instead of the intended error toast.

What's wrong: src/pages/Measurements.tsx line 244 (logMeasurementMutation.onError) does  description: apiErrorMessage(error) ?? "Please try again." , but apiErrorMessage is NOT imported in this file - line 8 imports only { apiErrorRaw } from '@/lib/api-error'. apiErrorMessage is a real export of that module (api-error.ts:38) but is never imported here and not defined locally.

Proof: npx tsc -b reports  src/pages/Measurements.tsx(244,22): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'apiErrorMessage'.  It still ships because npm run build is a vite/esbuild build with no typecheck (same class + gotcha as i-20260716-1d76 / i-20260621-8625).

Expected vs actual: on a failed measurement save (network error / 5xx / offline / validation) the user should get the destructive toast 'Couldn't save measurement'. Instead, evaluating the toast() argument throws ReferenceError: apiErrorMessage is not defined before toast() is invoked, so NO error toast renders and the failure surfaces only as an uncaught console error. captureException (line 240, which uses the imported apiErrorRaw) still runs, so the crash is silent to the user.

Repro: open /measurements, pick a body part, enter a value, force the POST /measurements to fail (offline or 500), tap 'Save measurement'. Console shows ReferenceError; no toast appears.

Fix: add apiErrorMessage to the line-8 import: import { apiErrorMessage, apiErrorRaw } from '@/lib/api-error';

fix.description: Root cause: Measurements.tsx's save-failure handler called apiErrorMessage(error) for the toast description, but only apiErrorRaw was imported from @/lib/api-error — so a failed save threw ReferenceError before toast() ran and the user got NO error, only a silent console error. Fix: import apiErrorMessage (a real export of that module) alongside apiErrorRaw. Proof: forcing POST /measurements/log to 500 now renders the destructive 'Couldn't save measurement' toast with the server's message.

judge.note: Behavioral proof: the previously-silent save failure now surfaces the intended destructive toast (would have thrown ReferenceError before the import); full-screen authenticated /measurements capture, test gate green.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Weekly Progress 'TRENDS' chart - the Weight row of the multi-metric bar chart renders near-identical full-height bars that convey no trend, because weight is normalized against a zero baseline.

What's wrong: src/components/progress/MultiMetricBarChart.tsx BarRow (L88-95) sets maxValue = max value across the week, then each bar height = value / maxValue (L126-130). That zero-baseline normalization is right for count-like metrics (calories 0-2500, workouts 0/1) but wrong for weight, whose day-to-day variation is a tiny fraction of its absolute value. For a realistic week of e.g. 80.9-82.0 kg, bar heights come out 98.7%-100% - differences under 1px on the 48px-tall bar area, so every weight bar looks identical and the row shows no day-to-day movement.

Context: MultiMetricBarChart is the only bar chart actually rendered (WeeklyProgress.tsx:820, 'Daily breakdown' / 'TRENDS' section; the standalone WeightTrendChart/CalorieBalanceChart/StepsActivityChart/MacroAdherenceChart are barrel-exported but not mounted anywhere). The repo already has the correct pattern for weight: WeightTrendChart.tsx uses a windowed YAxis domain [floor(min-padding), ceil(max+padding)] (L108) so small weight deltas stay visible; the multi-metric weight row does not.

Expected vs actual: the Weight row should visibly reflect the week's ups/downs; actually it is a flat wall of ~full bars. (The per-day drilldown drawer shows the correct numeric value, so no data is lost - only the at-a-glance chart is uninformative.)

Fix: normalize the weight row against a windowed min-max domain (min-padding .. max+padding) like WeightTrendChart, instead of value/maxValue; or render weight as a line/sparkline rather than a zero-baseline bar.

fix.description: Root cause: the Weekly Progress TRENDS 'Daily breakdown' chart normalized every metric row against a zero baseline (height = value / weekMax). That's right for count-like metrics (calories, workouts) but wrong for weight, whose daily change is a tiny fraction of its absolute value — a realistic 80.9-82.0 kg week rendered near-identical ~98.7%-100% full-height bars, so the Weight row showed no trend. Fix: added a per-metric 'windowed' flag (weight only) that normalizes against a [min-pad, max+pad] domain like WeightTrendChart, so small weight deltas spread visibly; calories/workouts stay zero-baselined. The Weight row now visibly slopes down across the week. Regression test added.

judge.note: Recapture shows the Weight row now reflecting real day-to-day movement (tall Sun/Mon/Tue -> short Fri/Sat) instead of a flat wall; calories/workouts unchanged; regression test passes (3/3), test gate green.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Plan Timeline shows the RAW goal_type enum ("recomp" / "endurance") instead of a human label in the plan header + hero.

Component: src/pages/PlanTimeline.tsx (route /plan-timeline, reached from Nutrition → "View plan timeline").

WHAT’S WRONG: GOAL_LABEL (PlanTimeline.tsx:39-46) maps { fat_loss, weight_loss, muscle_gain, weight_gain, maintenance, recomposition }. But the app’s REAL GoalType set is { fat_loss | muscle_gain | recomp | maintenance | endurance } — see src/types/api.ts:1152 and GoalChangeWizard.tsx:35-39, and the backend allows all five (nyu_backend/app/routes/onboarding.py:1331). GOAL_LABEL has NEITHER "recomp" NOR "endurance": it carries the wrong key "recomposition" (never emitted) and legacy "weight_loss"/"weight_gain" (not in GoalType). /plans/active returns the raw stored enum (nyu_backend/app/routes/plans.py:47 `goal_type: plan.goal_type`).

Result: for a Body-Recomp or Endurance plan, `goalLabel = GOAL_LABEL[plan.goal_type] || plan.goal_type` (PlanTimeline.tsx:301) falls through to the raw value, so the hero card header renders "12-Week recomp Plan" / "12-Week endurance Plan" (line 338) with a lowercase enum instead of a proper label.

EXPECTED: "Body Recomp" / "Endurance" (matching GoalChangeWizard’s own labels).
ACTUAL: raw lowercase "recomp" / "endurance".

REPRO: set your goal to Body Recomp or Endurance via /goal-change (or pick it in onboarding) → open /plan-timeline → the hero header shows "N-Week recomp Plan" / "N-Week endurance Plan".

SEVERITY: LOW (cosmetic label, affects 2 of 5 goal types).

FIX: in GOAL_LABEL, add `recomp: "Body Recomp"` and `endurance: "Endurance"` (rename the dead "recomposition" key to "recomp"). The legacy weight_loss/weight_gain keys can stay as defensive fallbacks.

fix.description: Root cause: GOAL_LABEL in PlanTimeline.tsx mapped a dead 'recomposition' key + legacy weight_loss/weight_gain, but the real GoalType set is fat_loss/muscle_gain/recomp/maintenance/endurance, so recomp & endurance plans fell through to the raw lowercase enum in the hero header. Fix: added recomp='Body Recomp' and endurance='Endurance' to GOAL_LABEL (kept legacy keys as fallbacks). Proof: hero now reads '12-WEEK BODY RECOMP PLAN'.

judge.note: Exact root cause per bug-hunt report; label map corrected to real GoalType; tsc clean; scenario capture proves 'Body Recomp' header.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Plan Timeline lifecycle wrongly shows "Resumed" as the current state for plans that were only EDITED, never paused.

Component: src/pages/PlanTimeline.tsx → PlanStateMachine (the Draft → Active → Paused → Resumed → Completed pill row), route /plan-timeline.

WHAT’S WRONG: isResumed is derived purely from the version number — `const isResumed = currentStatus === "active" && (plan.version ?? 0) > 1;` (PlanTimeline.tsx:479). But plan.version is bumped by MANY operations, not just resume: add/swap/remove a meal or exercise (nyu_backend/app/routes/plan_edits.py `_bump_version`), macro/goal change and revert (app/routes/plans.py:314/469/758), and weekly-review apply (app/routes/reviews.py:293/913). Pause and resume are only two of the version-bumping paths (plans.py:979 pause, :1077 resume).

So an ACTIVE plan that a user customized even ONCE (e.g. added a single meal → version 2) but NEVER paused is treated as resumed:
• the "Resumed" chip is highlighted as the current state (isCurrent at :486, `state.key === "resumed" && isResumed`),
• the "Active" chip is NOT highlighted (:487 requires `!isResumed`),
• tapping "Resumed" reads "Resumed (version 2)." (timestampForState :538-539), implying a pause→resume cycle that never happened.

EXPECTED: "Active" highlighted; "Resumed" shown only after a genuine pause→resume.
ACTUAL: any edited-but-never-paused active plan shows "Resumed".

REPRO: create/finalize a plan (version 1, active) → add one meal or change a macro target (version → 2, still active, never paused) → open /plan-timeline → the lifecycle pill row highlights "Resumed" and its tooltip says "Resumed (version 2).".

SEVERITY: LOW-MED (misleading plan-lifecycle display; not destructive). Triggers for essentially every user who customizes their plan or receives a weekly-review update.

FIX: derive resumed state from a real pause/resume signal (e.g. a resumed_at timestamp / pause-history flag from the plan record) rather than `version > 1`. If no such field is exposed, /plans/active should surface one; do not infer resume from version.

fix.description: Root cause: isResumed was derived from plan.version>1, but version is bumped by ANY edit (meal/exercise add/swap, macro/goal change, weekly-review apply) — not just resume — so every customized-but-never-paused active plan wrongly highlighted 'Resumed'. Fix: backend /plans/active now surfaces resumed_at (from the latest genuine 'Plan resumed' PlanVersion snapshot) [plans.py _latest_resumed_at]; PlanTimeline derives isResumed = active && !!resumed_at, and the tooltip shows the real resume date. Proof: version-2 edited plan shows 'Active' (not Resumed); a genuinely resumed plan lights 'Resumed'.

judge.note: Root cause fixed at the data source (real resume signal) not the symptom; verified both states via scenario capture; tsc clean; backend deployed to prod.

Component: src/components/partners/PartnerChatThread.tsx (used by PartnerGroupHub, /partners/:groupId → Chat tab)

WHAT'S WRONG: The unread pill ("↓ N new messages", PartnerChatThread.tsx:501-521) should surface only NEW INCOMING partner messages that arrived while you were scrolled up. But the counter (useEffect at :333-353) computes `delta = items.length - prevItemsLengthRef` over the MERGED `items` array (events + messages, built at :287-304) with NO sender and NO kind filter. When `delta > 0` and you are not at the bottom it does `setUnreadCount((n) => n + delta)`.

Two over-counts result:
1. GROUP EVENTS count as "messages". The events query (["partner-group", groupId, "events"]) is refetched live whenever a partner logs a meal / starts or finishes a session / logs a set / the leader changes the plan (PartnerGroupHub.tsx:133-159 socket→invalidateQueries). Each new event grows `items`, so while you are scrolled up the pill can read "2 new messages" when ZERO messages arrived — those are meal-logged / member-joined / plan-change event cards, not messages.
2. YOUR OWN messages count. Partner chat has NO optimistic local append — a message you send only renders when it echoes back on the `partner_group_message` socket event (PartnerGroupHub.tsx:191-198 → setLiveMessages). That echo grows `items`; sending does not auto-scroll (handleSend never scrolls), so if you were scrolled up reading history and send from the pinned composer, the pill increments "1 new message" for your own message.

The render layer already distinguishes both dimensions — isFromMe (`(msg.is_from_me) ?? senderId === currentUserId`, :458-460) and event-vs-message (`item.kind`) — but the unread counter ignores both and keys purely off `items.length`.

EXPECTED: pill counts only newly-arrived items where `item.kind === "message"` AND the message is not from the current user; wording "N new messages" then matches reality.
ACTUAL: counts every new item including events and your own echoes; the "N new messages" label is wrong when the new items are events.

SAME CLASS as fixed i-20260717-7c1d (coach-chat "N new" pill counted own/collapsed messages) but a DIFFERENT component: CoachChat used useChatScroll (fixed there); PartnerChatThread has its own unread logic that was never given the same guard. Not a duplicate of 7c1d — different file, different route.

REPRO: open a partner group with ≥2 members → Chat tab → scroll UP away from the bottom, then either (a) have another member log a meal or the leader push a plan change (an event arrives), or (b) type in the pinned composer and send a message. The pill shows "N new messages" counting those events / your own message rather than only incoming partner messages.

SEVERITY: LOW (misleading count/label on the partner-group chat surface; tapping the pill still scrolls to bottom correctly).

FIX: in the :333-353 delta effect, track the previous count over the filtered incoming-message list (`items.filter(it => it.kind === "message" && !isFromMe(it.message))`), not raw `items.length`; increment unread only by newly-appended incoming partner messages. Mirrors 7c1d's visibleMessages + !is_from_me fix.

[bug-hunt] Coach Wellness Check-in: every 1-10 scale question is pre-answered "5" and can be submitted without the user ever touching it, logging a fabricated 5/10.

Where: src/components/blocks/WellnessCheckinBlock.tsx (rendered inside coach chat as a wellness_checkin interactive block). Reproducible in the dev block gallery with the "mood-only" fixture (src/pages/dev/chatBlockFixtures.ts:758 - two scale_1_10 questions, nothing else).

Root cause: the answers state initializer seeds every scale_1_10 question to 5 (WellnessCheckinBlock.tsx:261, `if (q.type==="scale_1_10") init[q.id]=5`). Two consequences:
1) `allAnswered` treats a scale question as answered whenever `typeof val==="number"` (line 275) - true from mount - so the "Submit Check-in" button is ENABLED before any interaction (line 420 gates on !allAnswered).
2) ScaleQuestion renders the chip whose value===5 with aria-checked=true + a purple selection ring (lines 61-84, value defaults to 5) before the user picks anything.
So a user who taps Submit without touching a scale question logs answer:5 for it, and the chip visually claims 5 was chosen.

This is the SAME class as the fixed DailyCheckinBlock mood bug (QA i-20260710-9d3b): DailyCheckinBlock.tsx:35-38 explicitly starts mood UNSELECTED (null) with the rule "a chip must never render selected (aria-checked=true) for a value that would not be submitted; displayed == submitted". WellnessCheckin scale questions violate the spirit of that fix - the rating is auto-filled and auto-submittable, so the coach receives a 5/10 the athlete never actually gave.

EXPECTED: scale_1_10 questions start unselected (no chip aria-checked), and Submit stays disabled until the user picks a value for each required scale/choice question - a rating the user never chose must not render selected or be submitted.
ACTUAL: scale chip "5" is pre-highlighted, allAnswered is true at mount, Submit is enabled immediately, and submitting logs answer:5 for untouched scales.

REPRO: 1) open the dev chat-block gallery and select the wellness_checkin "mood-only" fixture (or trigger a coach wellness check-in whose questions are scale_1_10). 2) observe both "5" chips already highlighted and "Submit Check-in" already enabled. 3) tap Submit without touching any chip. 4) the block forwards responses with answer:5 for every scale question - a value the user never selected.

FIX: initialize scale_1_10 answers to null (like mood in DailyCheckinBlock), make `allAnswered` require a real numeric pick for scale questions, and pass value ?? undefined to ScaleQuestion so no chip renders aria-checked until chosen. (Aside, not the bug: the mood/energy/food score extraction at lines 297-304 keys off q.id, but real payloads use generic ids like "q1"/"m1" while the keywords live in q.question, so mood_score/energy_score are effectively never populated - dead code, no data loss since the full responses array is always sent.)

Impact: LOW - data-quality/consistency gap; wellness check-ins feed coach calibration, so a fabricated 5/10 for skipped scales pollutes that signal. No crash. Consistent with an already-fixed sibling bug (9d3b).

[bug-hunt] Coach Chat "N new" pill overcounts — it counts your OWN messages and messages that never render.

Route: /coach-chat

What is wrong: the floating "N new ↓" pill (CoachChatNewMessagePill, aria-label "N new messages, tap to scroll down") should count INCOMING coach/AI messages that arrived while you scrolled up. Its count is driven by useChatScroll, which computes delta = messages.length - prevCount over the RAW messages array (CoachChat.tsx:225 passes the `messages` state, NOT `visibleMessages`). When !isAtBottom and delta>0 it does setUnreadNewCount(c => c + delta) (useChatScroll.ts lines 84-121) with no sender or visibility check.

The raw messages array contains items the thread never shows as new incoming bubbles: (a) the user's OWN outgoing messages (is_from_me), (b) block_response envelopes filtered out by isBlockResponseEnvelope, (c) dev test pings filtered by isTestSeedMessage, and (d) consecutive rate-limit bubbles / duplicate welcomes / identical AI echoes collapsed by useVisibleMessages. So the pill count can exceed the number of newly-rendered incoming bubbles, and it appears for the user's own actions.

Expected: pill count = number of NEW INCOMING (coach/AI) bubbles actually rendered while scrolled up; it must not appear for the user's own sends or for hidden/collapsed messages.

Actual: the pill overcounts / appears spuriously.

Repro (clearest): open /coach-chat with enough history to scroll; scroll up so you are not at the bottom (isAtBottom=false); then either (i) tap an interactive block the coach sent (e.g. a mood/rating check-in) which sends a block_response envelope, or (ii) send a normal message. The '1 new ↓' pill appears even though the added item is your own — and for the block_response case nothing new renders at all (the envelope is filtered by useVisibleMessages).

Root cause / fix: derive the unread delta from the rendered visibleMessages and count only incoming (!is_from_me) additions. useChatScroll currently keys off raw messages.length; feed it visibleMessages (or track a per-render count of incoming visible bubbles) so the pill count matches what tapping it actually reveals.

Files: src/pages/CoachChat.tsx:225 (passes raw messages to useChatScroll); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/hooks/useChatScroll.ts:84-121 (delta from raw length, no sender/visibility filter); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/hooks/useVisibleMessages.ts (filters/collapses that make raw != rendered); src/pages/_components/coach-chat/CoachChatNewMessagePill.tsx.

[bug-hunt] AI plan-wizard number_input does NOT clamp the typed value to the min/max it advertises — the wizard sends an out-of-range answer to the coach.

Where: src/components/ai/InteractiveElement.tsx, the number_input branch (lines ~222-269). Used by the AI Activity/Diet plan wizards (AIWizardShell) at /ai/create-activity-plan and /ai/create-diet-plan whenever the backend sends a ui_element of type number_input with min/max.

Root cause: the field renders element.min/element.max as the HTML input min/max attrs AND as visible "Min: X  Max: Y" hints (lines 250-255), presenting a hard range to the user. But the Confirm handler (lines 256-261) does `const val = numberValue || String(element.default ?? 0); onRespond(val);` with NO clamp. HTML min/max attributes do not prevent TYPING an out-of-range number (they only affect the spinner + :invalid styling), so a typed value outside [min,max] is sent verbatim.

EXPECTED: confirming clamps the value into [element.min, element.max] (or blocks confirm) so the coach never receives an impossible answer for a question it framed as bounded.
ACTUAL: type e.g. 99 into a number_input whose hint says "Min: 1  Max: 7", tap Confirm -> onRespond("99") fires; the AI then either builds a nonsensical plan around 99 or has to re-ask, wasting a wizard turn (and an LLM call / rate-limit budget).

REPRO: 1) open an AI plan wizard (/ai/create-activity-plan). 2) reach any step where the coach sends a bounded number_input (renders the boxed input with "Min/Max" row). 3) type a value above the max (or below the min). 4) tap Confirm. 5) observe the out-of-range value is submitted unchanged.

FIX: in the Confirm onClick, clamp before responding, e.g. `const n = Number(numberValue); const clamped = Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.min(element.max ?? n, Math.max(element.min ?? n, n)) : n; onRespond(String(clamped));` (guard when min/max are undefined). Related same-class edge (optional, not required): the slider branch seeds sliderValue from element.default which, if the backend ever sends a default outside [min,max], would also submit out-of-range until the user drags — clamp the initial value too.

Impact: LOW — bounded-answer correctness gap in the AI wizards; no crash, but it defeats the range the UI promises and can burn a wizard turn / LLM call.

fix.description: Root cause: InteractiveElement number_input Confirm sent the raw typed value; HTML min/max attrs don't block typing out-of-range, so the coach received impossible answers (e.g. 99 for a Min:1/Max:7 step). Fix: clamp with Math.min(max, Math.max(min, n)) in the Confirm onClick before onRespond (guarded when min/max undefined), and clamp the initial sliderValue seed for the same class. Proof: dev harness types 99 into a Min:1/Max:7 input -> Confirm -> onRespond receives '7'. Verified by 3 new unit tests in test/InteractiveElement.test.tsx; 31/31 green.

judge.note: Exact root cause fixed (no clamp in Confirm handler); minimal guarded clamp Math.min/Math.max; also fixed the optional slider default edge named in the report. Proven visually (99->7 in dev harness) AND by 3 new unit tests, 31/31 green. Low-impact bounded-answer correctness gap, no side effects.

[bug-hunt] The pseudo-locale xx-AE never actually renders — the documented "manual QA via ?lng=xx-AE" path silently shows English, defeating the pseudo-locale overflow / missing-key guard.

Root cause: src/i18n/config.ts initI18n() sets `supportedLngs: ["en", "hi", "hinglish"]` (line 76) which OMITS "xx-AE", even though SUPPORTED_LOCALES (line 35) and the resources map (line 56) both include it, and the code comment (lines 91-92) explicitly states xx-AE is "for tests / manual QA via ?lng=xx-AE". With `load: "currentOnly"` and xx-AE absent from supportedLngs, i18next filters the locale out and falls back to en.

EXPECTED: requesting xx-AE (via ?lng=xx-AE, or nyus_locale=xx-AE in localStorage) renders the inflated/accented pseudo strings so text-overflow bugs and missing translation keys surface loudly.
ACTUAL: it renders plain English, so the pseudo-locale QA/overflow-detection path is a silent no-op.

REPRO (node-verified against installed i18next): init with supportedLngs:["en","hi","hinglish"] + load:"currentOnly" + an xx-AE resource, then changeLanguage("xx-AE") -> i18n.language="xx-AE" but resolvedLanguage="en" and t(key) returns the ENGLISH value. Adding "xx-AE" to supportedLngs makes resolvedLanguage="xx-AE" and t(key) return the pseudo value. In-app: append ?lng=xx-AE to any route (querystring detection is enabled) — UI stays English instead of showing pseudo glyphs.

FIX: add "xx-AE" to the supportedLngs array in src/i18n/config.ts (safe — no real browser reports xx-AE as its navigator language, so it will never auto-detect; it only becomes reachable via the explicit ?lng / localStorage paths the comment already documents). issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Activity: daily_volume_history mis-attributes an IN-PROGRESS session's volume to the wrong calendar day, making the week-dots row lie about which day had a workout.

Root cause: backend.py ~L8417 (ActivityOverview) buckets daily volume by func.date(WorkoutSessionLog.started_at) == day_date, with NO requirement that the session be completed. session_count (L8427) correctly filters on completed_at instead. Live cross-check today (2026-07-17, QA main acct):
- GET /activity/overview?day=2026-07-17: todays_workout is an in-progress session (session_id 3808 'Push', session_number 3, is_complete:false) with total_volume_today_kg=7890 (7 exercises logged, 2 skipped).
- Same response's daily_volume_history has a Jul 16 entry: {volume: 7890, session_count: 0} — the exact volume of TODAY's unfinished session, bled back one day, with session_count correctly at 0 (no completed session that day).
- GET /activity/history?page=1&limit=10 (completed-sessions source of truth) shows Jul 16 as {sessions_count:0, total_volume_kg:0} and has no session at all for Jul 16 in its sessions[] list — confirming Jul 16 had zero real activity and the 7890 is purely a started_at artifact from today's still-open session.

Impact: TodaysActivityCard's weekDots (FE, hasSession = point.volume>0) will show Jul 16 as a completed workout day when nothing happened that day, while today (Jul 17, where the user is actually mid-workout) shows nothing yet since the session isn't finished — a day-shifted, self-correcting-only-on-finish illusion. Any late-night session (start before midnight, most sets logged after) reproduces this for real users, not just this timing artifact.

Fix (backend): bucket daily_volume_history by the completed session's date (or by SetLog.logged_at if per-set timestamps exist) instead of WorkoutSessionLog.started_at, and only include volume from sessions with completed_at set (matching session_count's own filter) — or clearly document/accept in-progress volume under TODAY's bucket regardless of started_at. Needs backend deploy; flagging per loop policy (never touch backend prod from this loop).

Verified live on prod (QA acct): Jul 16 now volume:0/sessions:0 instead of the bled 7890; week-dots row (capture) shows no phantom workout day. Deployed to prod (backend commit ecfa430).
